I attached a short production profile (Arkship_production_profile.csv) and our SLO matrix. Short summary:

Emma — thanks for the data, this is exactly what we need to start. Quick take up front: we typically recommend a hybrid fleet for mixed long-context and high-concurrency short-turns. L4s buy you cost-effective concurrency on short requests; H100s are better for long-context retrieval-heavy flows (bigger KV cache / larger model memory), with A100 as a middle ground if you want fewer SKUs.

I'm attaching a short prelim note (prelim-sizing-note.docx) with a mapping exercise I ran against your CSV. Two asks before we finalize:

2) What fallback policy is acceptable to Arkship when Dedicated bursts above capacity (queueing vs degraded model / shorter context vs spillage to hosted)?

If you want, we can set a 30-min call this week to walk a proposed fleet mix and cost sensitivity.

Looping Dev + Infra for SKU-level tradeoffs. High-level technical notes for Arkship and procurement: 

1) Memory and context considerations- H100 (80GB HBM3 variant) — best for very large models / long KV caching and large sequence lengths. Enables fewer model sharding/fusion headaches; supports larger batch *and* long-context inference with reduced OOM risk.
- Typical use: RAG with 40k+ token contexts and p99-heavy workloads.

- A100 (80GB / 40GB variants) — good compromise; fewer SKUs are supported across cloud vendors. If you standardize on A100-80GB you get decent long-context capability but may need more cards for throughput.

- L4 (24GB GDDR6-like) — optimized for cost and concurrent QPS on shorter contexts. Great when you can quantize (INT8/4) and use smaller segment sizes; limited for 40k contexts unless you run retrieval server-side and send distilled context.

2) Performance per token / throughput tradeoffs (rules of thumb)- H100: best tokens/sec for large-context models and FP16/AMP paths; higher per-card cost but fewer cards for heavy long-context jobs.- A100: solid single-card throughput for many open models; middle-of-road price.- L4: higher aggregate concurrency per dollar for short-turns, but limited KV cache and memory headroom.

3) Inference patterns & autoscale policies- Map flows to SKUs: long-RAG -> H100 pool; mid-length batch jobs (document ingest / offline embed) -> A100 / spare H100; short-turn interactive summarization -> L4 pool with aggressive batching.
- Reserve a small H100 buffer for degraded failover (e.g., when a long-RAG request arrives and H100s are saturated, we can fall back to an A100 with reduced context or to a shorter-context model bundle).

4) Operational recommendation (initial reserved footprint)- Proposed reserved mix for Arkship (sustained coverage + 30% autoscale headroom):
  - H100 (80GB) x 6 — dedicated to long-context RAG generation and p95 latency-sensitive calls.
  - L4 x 18 — handle bulk short-turn summarization with batching and quantized models.
  - A100 x 4 (optional) — shared buffer for medium-length jobs and as fallback when H100s are saturated.

Estimated rationale: this mix supports your 120 peak QPS with low-p50 latency by segregating workloads, reduces per-token cost via L4 batching, and keeps H100s to avoid context trimming on long jobs. I attached a sku-comparison-table.csv with memory/perf numbers and an initial cost sensitivity.

Questions for Arkship / Procurement:
- Is model quantization acceptable for the short-turn flow (INT8 / 4-bit)?
- Are you open to a small A100 pool instead of A100s if vendor availability is constrained?

Happy to convert this to a slide deck for procurement.

— Lauren
